::: {#thm-biconditional-split}
#### A biconditional is two conditionals

For propositions $P$ and $Q$,

$$
(P \Leftrightarrow Q) \equiv \paren{(P \Rightarrow Q) \land (Q \Rightarrow P)}.
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

The fourth and last columns of this truth table (@def-truth-table) match in every row
(@def-iff, @def-implies, @def-and):

| $P$ | $Q$ | $P \Rightarrow Q$ | $Q \Rightarrow P$ | $(P \Rightarrow Q) \land (Q \Rightarrow P)$ | $P \Leftrightarrow Q$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| T | T | T | T | T | T |
| T | F | F | T | F | F |
| F | T | T | F | F | F |
| F | F | T | T | T | T |

So the two propositions are logically equivalent (@def-logical-equivalence).

:::

:::
